proposals.before: It is tempting to translate that arrangement into a modern contract: everything that follows must be derived from exactly these clauses, and no other resource may be used. That translation expresses a later ideal of explicit axiomatization. The ancient text does not itself present a fully specified formal language, inference calculus, or prohibition on diagrammatic reasoning.
proposals.after: Later mathematicians would press the list harder: if these are the starting points, nothing else may slip in, however obvious it looks. Euclid had not shut diagrams out of the proof. But he had put the starting points on the page.
proposals.reason: 保留事实与证据边界，以散文承接作者已批准的中文；不添加新材料。

proposals.before: It is too strong to say that the operation is physically impossible in every conceivable setup. Its success depends on object size, adulteration, apparatus, and precision. The historically responsible criticism is that the familiar account does not establish a sufficiently controlled assay. A correct principle does not authenticate the episode or its procedure.
proposals.after: Could the procedure distinguish a genuine crown from an adulterated one? That depends on the crown, the mixture, the apparatus, and how precisely the water could be measured. The story gives us a sound principle. It leaves the reliability of the test much less clear.
proposals.reason: 保留事实与证据边界，以散文承接作者已批准的中文；不添加新材料。

proposals.before: To say that for two hundred and fifty years nobody offered any worthwhile explanation would erase Wallis and the other interpretive efforts already described. What remained absent for much of the interval was a broadly accepted, systematically coordinated account, not every meaningful idea.
proposals.after: For more than two centuries the calculations went on, and explanations grew alongside them. Wallis and others had offered ways of understanding the unfamiliar quantities. But what reassured one mathematician did not necessarily reassure the next. Calculation, explanation, and acceptance did not keep the same pace.
proposals.reason: 保留事实与证据边界，以散文承接作者已批准的中文；不添加新材料。

proposals.before: Our earlier discussion of an alleged ancient crisis warned against reading later stories back into periods without contemporary evidence. Here contemporary evidence is abundant: letters, an appendix, articles, and new axiom systems. The lesson cannot be that no crisis occurred. It must be a more exact account of what was endangered, who was involved, and when the language of crisis entered the discussion.
proposals.after: The ancient crisis described earlier became more vivid with each retelling, but no voice from the time survives to tell us of that upheaval. Whether it happened at all remains uncertain. This time there is paper: letters, an appendix, articles, and new axiom systems. We have to ask what was shaken, whose work was threatened, and when they began to call it a crisis.
proposals.reason: 保留事实与证据边界，以散文承接作者已批准的中文；不添加新材料。

proposals.before: The earlier discussion of an ancient mathematical crisis and the present one should not receive the same verdict. In the ancient case, there is no contemporary documentary basis for a community-wide collapse over incommensurability. Late stories of punishment or drowning do exist, but their lateness and variation prevent them from establishing the familiar dramatic reconstruction. Here the documents are contemporary and direct.
proposals.after: The earlier crisis leaves us wondering whether it happened at all. The incommensurable lines are real enough. The collapse they supposedly brought about has left no paper from its own time. Stories of punishment and drowning came much later; the story of a sweeping crisis came later still. This time, the people caught in the argument left their own words.
proposals.reason: 保留事实与证据边界，以散文承接作者已批准的中文；不添加新材料。

proposals.before: This is a different historical operation from simply removing an unsupported story. It redraws the boundaries of a well-documented event. The absence of universal panic does not imply the absence of intellectual danger; the failure of Frege's scheme does not imply the failure of every theorem proved in analysis. Keeping those distinctions visible is part of taking the crisis seriously.
proposals.after: That legendary crisis may never have happened. This one did, but it reached less far than the familiar story suggests. The two corrections can look alike. They are not. One asks whether the story happened; the other redraws the boundaries of something real. Frege's foundations could fail without bringing down every theorem in analysis. The second story is harder to tell, because it offers no clean sweep.
proposals.reason: 保留事实与证据边界，以散文承接作者已批准的中文；不添加新材料。

proposals.before: Two gaps remain in this account's chronology. War stopped Tarski's planned Paris book. Genocide ended Presburger's life, leaving its final date uncertain. Those are not limitations of a formal language. They are losses inflicted on the people who built one. The next episode returns to the institutions from which people could be removed while the mathematical symbols remained.
proposals.after: War kept a book out of the printing house and cut short the life of a mathematician. The manuscript was recovered. Presburger's last days left only a year with a question mark beside it. The next episode turns the clock back to 1933, and to a university.
proposals.reason: 保留事实与证据边界，以散文承接作者已批准的中文；不添加新材料。
